metadata.title: Scientific BMR & Energy Expenditure Calculator
metadata.description: Evidence-based calculation of Basal Metabolic Rate and TDEE using Mifflin-St Jeor and Katch-McArdle models.

header.title: BMR & TDEE Calculator
header.subtitle: Energy expenditure estimates grounded in peer-reviewed physiological literature.

mifflin.title: Mifflin-St Jeor (1990)
mifflin.description: Recommended by the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics for the general population when body fat is unknown.

katch.title: Katch-McArdle (1996)
katch.description: Estimates BMR based on Fat-Free Mass (FFM). Superior accuracy for athletes and resistance-trained individuals with known body fat percentage.

bodyFat.label: Body Fat (BF)
bodyFat.hint: Obtained via bioimpedance analysis, calipers, or DXA scan.

sedentary.label: Sedentary (1.20)
sedentary.description: Desk job, passive commuting, little to no planned exercise.

light.label: Lightly Active (1.375)
light.description: Desk job paired with light/moderate workouts 1 to 3 days per week or active daily walking.

moderate.label: Moderately Active (1.55)
moderate.description: Resistance training, CrossFit, or moderate-to-high intensity sports 3 to 5 days per week.

very_active.label: Very Active (1.725)
very_active.description: Intense training 6 to 7 days per week, or a physically demanding job with routine exercise.

extra_active.label: Extremamente Active (1.90)
extra_active.description: Competitive athletes, two-a-day training regimens, or heavy physical labor.

bmr.label: Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)
bmr.description: Calories required to sustain vital physiological organs at absolute resting state.

tdee.label: Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE)
tdee.description: Estimated calories required to maintain body weight at your current activity level.

confidenceInterval.label: Physiological Uncertainty Interval (±10%)
confidenceInterval.tooltip: Population formulas carry inherent variability due to mitochondrial efficiency, TEF, and spontaneous NEAT.

scientificNotes.title: Methodological Note
scientificNotes.content: Predictive equations represent population statistical models. Indirect calorimetry remains the gold standard for clinical measurement.

weight.min: Weight must be at least 20 kg.

height.min: Height must be at least 50 cm.
